extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of literature, poets, and those interested in creative/philosophical aphorisms
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Blake's aphoristic 'Proverbs of Hell' and associated didactic passages offering prescriptive statements about perception, poetry, genius, desire, and conduct—intended as guidance for poets, prophets, and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrary 1: unity of body and soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Man has no Body distinct from his Soul. For that called Body is a portion of Soul discerned by the five senses, the chief inlets of Soul in this age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrary 2: energy as life and reason as boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy is the only life, and is from the Body; and Reason is the bound or outward circumference of Energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrary 3: energy as eternal delight
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy is Eternal Delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: On restraint of desire
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who restrain desire, do so because theirs is weak enough to be restrained; and the restrainer or reason usurps its place and governs the unwilling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied guidance: do not valorize the restraining of desire as morally superior; restraint indicates weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: The voice of honest indignation
rubrics_metrics.description: The voice of honest indignation is the voice of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In context (Isaiah): be willing to write from honest indignation even if misunderstood; conviction justifies prophetic poetic speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Does a firm persuasion that a thing is so, make it so? All poets believe that it does, and in ages of imagination this firm persuasion removed mountains;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for poets: a firm imaginative conviction can effect change; belief shapes poetic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doors of perception
rubrics_metrics.description: If the doors of perception were cleansed everything would appear to man as it is, infinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative directive: purify perception to perceive the infinite; a poet's task is to reveal infinite aspects hidden by narrow senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animate sensible objects and study their genius
rubrics_metrics.description: The ancient poets animated all sensible objects with Gods or Geniuses, calling them by the names and adorning them with properties of woods, rivers, mountains ... they studied the Genius of each city and country, placing it under its mental deity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic method: personify and discover the 'genius' of places/objects rather than abstracting them away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: In seed-time learn, in harvest teach, in winter enjoy.
rubrics_metrics.description: In seed-time learn, in harvest teach, in winter enjoy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aphoristic lifecycle guideline for learning, teaching, and enjoyment; no further elaboration in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Drive your cart and your plough over the bones of the dead.
rubrics_metrics.description: Drive your cart and your plough over the bones of the dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive aphorism advocating boldness and disregard for past constraints or dead authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: The road of excess
rubrics_metrics.description: The road of excess leads to the palace of wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorses experiential excess as a path to insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Prudence critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Prudence is a rich ugly old maid courted by Incapacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical of excessive prudence; implies prudence may hinder creative capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Desire must be acted upon
rubrics_metrics.description: He who desires, but acts not, breeds pestilence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates acting on desire; inaction corrupts or causes harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: The cut worm forgives the plough.
rubrics_metrics.description: The cut worm forgives the plough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous aphorism; suggests resilience or acceptance of necessary harm in processes of growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Dip him in the river who loves water.
rubrics_metrics.description: Dip him in the river who loves water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literal-seeming hyperbole encouraging immersion in what one loves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Perception differs by wisdom
rubrics_metrics.description: A fool sees not the same tree that a wise man sees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perceptual guidance: wisdom changes what is perceived in the same object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Face giving no light
rubrics_metrics.description: He whose face gives no light shall never become a star.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphor for lacking inner radiance or genius; won't achieve prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Eternity and productions of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Eternity is in love with the productions of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing temporal creations as beloved by the eternal; support for valuing temporal art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: The busy bee
rubrics_metrics.description: The busy bee has no time for sorrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: productive engagement avoids sorrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Hours of folly vs wisdom
rubrics_metrics.description: The hours of folly are measured by the clock, but of wisdom no clock can measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wisdom is beyond conventional measurement of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: All wholesome food is caught without a net or a trap.
rubrics_metrics.description: All wholesome food is caught without a net or a trap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests that what is wholesome comes freely, not by artifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Bring out number, weight, and measure in dearth
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring out number, weight, and measure in a year of dearth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In scarcity, quantify and measure resources carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Self-reliant soaring
rubrics_metrics.description: No bird soars too high if he soars with his own wings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates self-reliance in ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: A dead body revenges not injuries
rubrics_metrics.description: A dead body revenges not injuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation about futility of posthumous revenge; ethical implication: do not rely on inaction for justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Most sublime act is to set another before you
rubrics_metrics.description: The most sublime act is to set another before you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral guidance: selflessness is exalted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Fool persisting becomes wise
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fool would persist in his folly he would become wise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paradoxical guidance: persistence (even in folly) can lead to insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Folly as cloak of knavery
rubrics_metrics.description: Folly is the cloak of knavery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning that foolishness may be used to disguise deceit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Shame is Pride's cloak
rubrics_metrics.description: Shame is Pride's cloak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous moral observation on emotions and social presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Prisons and brothels
rubrics_metrics.description: Prisons are built with stones of law, brothels with bricks of religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical observation: institutions of law and religion can be used oppressively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Pride of peacock
rubrics_metrics.description: The pride of the peacock is the glory of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms natural proud display as part of divine glory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Lust of the goat
rubrics_metrics.description: The lust of the goat is the bounty of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms natural desire as part of divine bounty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Wrath of the lion
rubrics_metrics.description: The wrath of the lion is the wisdom of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural ferocity seen as part of divine wisdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Nakedness of woman
rubrics_metrics.description: The nakedness of woman is the work of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms natural human form as divine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Excessive emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess of sorrow laughs, excess of joy weeps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paradox: extreme emotions contain their opposites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Natural forces as portions of Eternity
rubrics_metrics.description: The roaring of lions, the howling of wolves, the raging of the stormy sea, and the destructive sword, are portions of Eternity too great for the eye of man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize natural/destructive forces as aspects of an overwhelming eternal reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Fox condemns the trap
rubrics_metrics.description: The fox condemns the trap, not himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation on blame-shifting and self-deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Joys and sorrows reproductive metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Joys impregnate, sorrows bring forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphor indicating creative productivity from joy and birth from sorrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Dress in strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Let man wear the fell of the lion, woman the fleece of the sheep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphorical counsel about adopting qualities appropriate to one's nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Animal homes and human friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: The bird a nest, the spider a web, man friendship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines friendship as humanity's defining construct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Fools thought wise to be a rod
rubrics_metrics.description: The selfish smiling fool and the sullen frowning fool shall be both thought wise that they may be a rod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cynical observation on how social perception can be manipulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: What is proved was once imagined
rubrics_metrics.description: What is now proved was once only imagined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages imaginative hypothesis as precursor to proof; a creativity/innovation guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Root vs fruit watchers
rubrics_metrics.description: The rat, the mouse, the fox, the rabbit watch the roots; the lion, the tiger, the horse, the elephant watch the fruits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphoric division of creatures by their focus—suggests different natures and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Cistern vs fountain
rubrics_metrics.description: The cistern contains, the fountain overflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast between containment and abundance; creative implication: overflow is generative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: One thought fills immensity
rubrics_metrics.description: One thought fills immensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The power of a single, expansive idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Speak your mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Always be ready to speak your mind, and a base man will avoid you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages frankness as a social filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Believability and truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything possible to be believed is an image of truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the relation between plausibility and representation of truth; poetic license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: The eagle and the crow
rubrics_metrics.description: The eagle never lost so much time as when he submitted to learn of the crow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning against wasting time on lesser models when one has greater capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Fox vs God for provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The fox provides for himself, but God provides for the lion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference between cunning self-provision and ordained provision for the mighty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Daily pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Think in the morning, act in the noon, eat in the evening, sleep in the night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive daily regimen aligning mental and physical activities with times of day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: He who has suffered you to impose on him
rubrics_metrics.description: He who has suffered you to impose on him knows you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On reputation: those who tolerate imposition will recognize character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: As the plough follows words
rubrics_metrics.description: As the plough follows words, so God rewards prayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy linking speech/action and divine reward; implications for sincerity in speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Tigers of wrath
rubrics_metrics.description: The tigers of wrath are wiser than the horses of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing passionate, instinctive energy over formal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Expect poison from standing water
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect poison from the standing water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical warning against stagnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Knowing enough
rubrics_metrics.description: You never know what is enough unless you know what is more than enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To understand sufficiency one must exceed it; a paradoxical test of limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Listen to the fool's reproach
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to the fool's reproach; it is a kingly title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take heed of criticism from unexpected sources; humility in listening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Elements as senses
rubrics_metrics.description: The eyes of fire, the nostrils of air, the mouth of water, the beard of earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic mapping of senses/elements; poetic imagery to guide symbolic thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Weakness in courage
rubrics_metrics.description: The weak in courage is strong in cunning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation on compensatory traits; not an endorsement but a description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Apple tree/beech analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: The apple tree never asks the beech how he shall grow, nor the lion the horse how he shall take his prey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages following one's innate nature rather than seeking inappropriate models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Thankful receiver
rubrics_metrics.description: The thankful receiver bears a plentiful harvest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attitude of gratitude yields abundance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: If others had not been foolish
rubrics_metrics.description: If others had not been foolish we should have been so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection on collective folly and its role in shaping behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Soul of sweet delight
rubrics_metrics.description: The soul of sweet delight can never be defiled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assertion of the purity/persistence of joy or delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Eagle as portion of Genius
rubrics_metrics.description: When thou seest an eagle, thou seest a portion of Genius. Lift up thy head!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic correlation of natural grandeur with genius; exhortation to look up and recognize greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Priest curses fairest joys
rubrics_metrics.description: As the caterpillar chooses the fairest leaves to lay her eggs on, so the priest lays his curse on the fairest joys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of religious repression of natural pleasures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: To create a little flower
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a little flower is the labour of ages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing small creations as the product of long, profound effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Damn braces; bless relaxes.
rubrics_metrics.description: Damn braces; bless relaxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor looseness/relaxation over rigid constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Best wine and water
rubrics_metrics.description: The best wine is the oldest, the best water the newest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juxtaposition valuing aged refinement in some things and freshness in others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Prayers and praises ineffective metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Prayers plough not; praises reap not; joys laugh not; sorrows weep not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ironic statement on mismatches of expected effects and actual outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Head, heart, genitals, hands and feet
rubrics_metrics.description: The head Sublime, the heart Pathos, the genitals Beauty, the hands and feet Proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic/organological mapping of faculties to artistic values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Contempt simile
rubrics_metrics.description: As the air to a bird, or the sea to a fish, so is contempt to the contemptible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation on the contextuality of contempt; contempt is natural environment for the contemptible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Crow and owl wishes
rubrics_metrics.description: The crow wished everything was black; the owl that everything was white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire of ideological absolutism or binary thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Exuberance is Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Exuberance is Beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct aesthetic assertion: exuberance equals beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Lion advised by fox
rubrics_metrics.description: If the lion was advised by the fox, he would be cunning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel on the benefit of combining strengths (power + cunning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Improvement vs crooked roads
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvement makes straight roads, but the crooked roads without Improvement are roads of Genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts technocratic improvement with original, crooked genius; values originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Unacted desires
rubrics_metrics.description: Sooner murder an infant in its cradle than nurse unacted desires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radical injunction to act on desires rather than let them stagnate; extreme phrasing to emphasize creative urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Where man is not, nature is barren
rubrics_metrics.description: Where man is not, nature is barren.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthropocentric claim that human presence enlivens nature (poetic position).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Truth and belief
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth can never be told so as to be understood and not to be believed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the intimate link between understanding and belief in communicative truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proverb: Enough or Too much
rubrics_metrics.description: Enough! or Too much.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise aphorism asserting tension between sufficiency and excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic method: writing from senses finding infinite
rubrics_metrics.description: Isaiah: 'I saw no God, nor heard any, in a finite organical perception: but my senses discovered the infinite in everything; and as I was then persuaded, and remained confirmed, that the voice of honest indignation is the voice of God, I cared not for consequences, but wrote.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for prophetic/poetic practice: trust sensory discovery of the infinite and write from the persuasive conviction of indignation regardless of consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic origin principle (Ezekiel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ezekiel: 'We of Israel taught that the Poetic Genius ... was the first principle, and all the others merely derivative.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory for poets: prioritize the Poetic Genius as primary source; consider other systems derivative.

rubrics_metrics.name: On prophetic acts (Ezekiel's eccentric behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ezekiel's acts (going naked, eating dung, lying on sides) were performed 'The desire of raising other men into a perception of the infinite.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance by example: extreme prophetic acts may be intended to jolt perception and reveal the infinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imminent conflagration through sensual improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The ancient tradition that the world will be consumed in fire at the end of six thousand years is true... This will come to pass by an improvement of sensual enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests transformative social/cosmic change through expansion/improvement of sensual enjoyment—an aesthetic/political prescription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing-house allegory for transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of Hell's printing-house chambers shows stages: clearing rubbish, adorning cave, making inner infinite, melting metals into living fluids, casting forms into expanse, arranging in libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphor for stages of cultural/knowledge production: clearing, ornamenting, imagining, transforming, casting, arranging—an implied method for cultural transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of Swedenborg as superficial recapitulator
rubrics_metrics.description: Swedenborg 'has not written one new truth... he has written all the old falsehoods.' He conversed with Angels (religious) not Devils (who hate religion), thus limiting his insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical standard: original insight comes from engaging with contraries/energies (Devils) as well as religious thought; avoid mere recapitulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worship of God as honoring genius in others
rubrics_metrics.description: The worship of God is, honouring His gifts in other men each according to his genius, and loving the greatest men best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical/aesthetic guideline: recognize and honor genius in others proportionally; oppose envy/calumny.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Jesus and virtue beyond rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Devil's claim: 'no virtue can exist without breaking these ten commandments. Jesus was all virtue, and acted from impulse, not from rules.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provocative guideline: true virtue/creativity may come from impulse rather than strict adherence to rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: One law for the lion and ox is Oppression
rubrics_metrics.description: One law for the lion and ox is Oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political/ethical critique: one-size-fits-all law is oppressive to differing natures.
